Paragraph:
Translation: As the ignorant perform their duties with attachment to results, similarly the learned may also act, but without attachment, for the sake of leading people on the right path.

Purport (Excerpt): A person in Krsna consciousness and a person not in Krsna consciousness are differentiated by different desires... one is engaged in such activities for the satisfaction of his sense gratification, whereas the other is engaged for the satisfaction of Krsna... show the people how to act...
Situation/Problem_Faced: Understanding how a wise person acts in the world compared to an attached, ignorant person when their outward behaviors look identical.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna contrasts motivation: the ignorant act out of attachment to personal fruits, while the wise act with equal diligence but total detachment, working solely for social guidance and spiritual elevation.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna learns that spiritual maturity changes one's internal intent, not necessarily external productivity.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Internal Intent vs. External Action: Recognizing that psychological state is defined by underlying motive, not just physical effort
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Detached Diligence: Working with high focus and care without clinging to personal gain
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Altruistic Leadership: Executing daily responsibilities to guide and uplift others

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Saktah karmanvidvamso (The ignorant acting with strong attachment to fruits)
Kuryad vidvams tathasaktah (The wise acting with equal enthusiasm but total detachment)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: While unlearned people work driven by selfish attachment to results, self-realized individuals perform their duties with equal care and vigor, but completely unattached, acting purely to guide society along the path of righteousness.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Two people can perform the exact same job, but their mental states can be completely different. One works out of anxiety and selfish attachment, while the other works with inner peace and altruism. Changing your inner motivation transforms hard labor into fulfilling, stress-free action.
